lessons.mistake: Spent 4+ attempts trying to clean 96K iCloud emails via MCP (14/min), Python scripts (needs app password), Chrome UI search (crashes on 96K), and one-by-one deletion — when Apple's built-in 'iCloud Mail Cleanup' feature was visible in the sidebar the entire time.
lessons.rootCause: Defaulted to building custom tools instead of first checking if the platform already solves the problem. Engineer mindset overrode practical thinking.
lessons.correctApproach: ALWAYS check platform-native features FIRST before building custom solutions. iCloud Mail Cleanup → Settings → Cleanup deleted 10,000+ emails in minutes with 3 clicks. The feature also runs PERMANENTLY — no recurring maintenance.
lessons.rule: PLATFORM-FIRST: Before building ANY automation, spend 2 minutes checking if the target platform already has a built-in feature for it. Check settings menus, help docs, and web search '[platform] bulk [action]' before writing a single line of code.

lessons.mistake: Dedup agent searched iCloud IMAP for sent emails that were actually sent from Gmail (tomasmarty@bureauflow.io). Concluded '5 hot lead emails NOT SENT' when they were confirmed sent via Gmail at 10:57.
lessons.rootCause: Dedup agent lacks awareness of multi-account email topology. It only has access to iCloud MCP, not Gmail MCP. It searched the wrong account and reported a false negative.
lessons.correctApproach: Before declaring something 'not done', check ALL possible sources. Tomas has 4 email accounts (Gmail workspace, iCloud, Hotmail, Closers). The dedup agent should note which accounts it checked and flag uncertainty when it can't access all sources.
lessons.rule: MULTI-SOURCE VERIFICATION: When checking if an action was completed, explicitly state which data sources were checked and which were NOT accessible. Never declare 'NOT DONE' without acknowledging blind spots.

lessons.mistake: Security audit agent flagged Stripe/Google/Neon secrets in git history as needing rotation — but these were already rotated the previous week. Wasted Tomas's attention on a solved problem.
lessons.rootCause: Security agent scanned git history (which is immutable) and reported findings without checking dedup task history. The rotation was logged in completed-tasks.json but the security agent didn't consult it.
lessons.correctApproach: ALL agents should consult the dedup agent's completed-tasks.json BEFORE reporting findings. If a remediation was already done, say 'Previously resolved on [date]' instead of creating a new alert.
lessons.rule: CHECK-BEFORE-ALERT: Before flagging any issue, check completed-tasks.json for prior resolution. Report 'Resolved on [date]' instead of re-alerting on known-fixed issues.

lessons.mistake: FlowOps SENTINEL cron generated a '6 critical threats' alert that was mostly self-referential — its own previous alerts citing each other as threats. Tax Einspruch was already filed, 'missing Steuerberater' is Claude (per CFO mandate).
lessons.rootCause: SENTINEL scans inbox emails including its own previous alerts, creating a feedback loop. It lacks context about business rules (Claude = accountant, Einspruch = filed).
lessons.correctApproach: SENTINEL should exclude its own previous alerts from threat scanning (filter FROM: sentinel@flowops.bureauflow.de). It should also check completed-tasks.json for tax-related resolutions before alerting.
lessons.rule: NO-SELF-REFERENCE: Monitoring agents must exclude their own previous outputs from analysis to prevent feedback loops. Always filter out self-generated content.

lessons.mistake: Repeatedly asked 'What's next?' and declared 'Done!' instead of proactively finding and executing the next highest-impact action. CEO with ADHD needs autonomous execution, not status reports.
lessons.rootCause: Default assistant behavior is to wait for instructions. BureauFlow partnership requires deep autonomy — act first, report results, move to next action.
lessons.correctApproach: After completing any task: (1) check revenue pipeline, (2) check inbox for replies, (3) run evolve agent for improvements, (4) check for stale data. Never stop. Never ask 'what's next'.
lessons.rule: NEVER-IDLE: After completing a task, immediately identify and start the next highest-impact action. Prioritize: revenue > bugs > infrastructure > optimization. Report results inline, don't pause for approval.

lessons.mistake: Built 16 TypeScript files, 5,278 lines of agent code, self-improvement systems, proactive schedulers — while BureauFlow has 0 paying customers. The agents are impressive but don't directly generate revenue.
lessons.rootCause: Engineering is fun and feels productive. Revenue actions (posting Upwork job, sending comparison article emails, recording YouTube demo) require human execution and feel less satisfying.
lessons.correctApproach: At scale zero, every action should be measured by: 'Does this get us closer to customer #1?' Building agent infrastructure is P2. Sending the re-engagement email campaign, posting the Upwork job, and emailing comparison article editors are P0.
lessons.rule: REVENUE-FIRST AT SCALE ZERO: Until there is at least 1 paying customer, prioritize actions that directly drive signups and conversions over infrastructure improvements. Ask: 'Will this generate revenue this week?'
